discarded_from_v2: syntax variety for its own sake
avoidance of repeated openings as primary concern
Dynamic Movement / oscillation as preferred pattern

sections.purpose: Help a user understand the film’s emotional feel at a glance. Write like a thoughtful friend — clear and immediate — not like a film critic crafting a beautiful sentence.
core_principles: First-words test: can someone understand the basic mood from the first few words?
Name the mood clearly first, then add 1–2 specifics that make it more useful for this film.
Default shape: [Mood], with [1–2 specifics]. This is a default, not a hard template.
After naming the mood, say the most natural useful thing about THIS film: image, setting, sound, behavior, or distinctive contrast. Prefer what makes the film recognizable.

Do not fill the after-clause with batch-common medium labels. In a batch of mostly 2D films, "with rough/soft/vivid 2D animation" is usually interchangeable filler — skip it unless the technique itself is unusual or truly shapes the feel (e.g. stop-motion puppets, rotoscope, stark black-and-white).
Mention pace only when pace itself is central to the experience — not as a default intensifier.
Simple repeated sentence shapes are normal. Adj openings are normal. Structural uniformity is not a problem.
Prefer natural, simple English. Imagery only when it is the clearest phrasing — never critic prose.
Do not retell the synopsis or explain the film’s themes.

mood_dimensions.name: Core mood
mood_dimensions.detail: The main emotional feel, named early.

mood_dimensions.name: Useful specifics
mood_dimensions.detail: Film-owned cues first: setting, image, sound, behavior, distinctive contrast. Technique only when unusual or feel-defining. Pace only when central. Avoid default medium labels shared by most films in the batch.

strong_patterns.why: Point to something this film owns — place, image, behavior — not a shared medium label.
Easy to read; no critic performance.

weak_patterns.when_weak: Mood opening followed by interchangeable filler: slow/fast/energetic pacing, quiet moments, dark tension, bleak atmosphere, vibes.
weak_patterns.when_ok: When pace/silence/tension is distinctive for this film and paired with a recognizable cue.

weak_patterns.when_weak: After-clause defaults to "with [adj] 2D animation…" (or similar batch-common medium) when almost every film shares that technique. Sounds concrete but is interchangeable.
weak_patterns.when_ok: When technique is distinctive (stop-motion puppets, rotoscope, stark B&W, unusual hybrid) and naming it helps the feel.

weak_patterns.pattern: Visual/technique lead that delays the mood
weak_patterns.when_weak: First words describe medium before emotional feel.
weak_patterns.when_ok: Rarely; only if that cue is the fastest mood signal.

weak_patterns.when_weak: Written to impress; stacked metaphors; review-copy cadence.

weak_patterns.pattern: Empty generic mood with no film cue

syntax_library.principle: Start with the mood, then a concrete film-owned cue. Example: 'Dreamy and nostalgic, with soft pastel Florida suburbia and sudden surreal daydreams.' Do not default to 'with soft 2D animation…'.

sections.specificity_test: Do the first few words name the mood? Easy on first read? At least one cue this film owns? Could the after-clause move to another film in the same batch and still fit? If yes — especially if it only says 2D animation / pacing / moments — replace it.
sections.relationship_with_synopsis: Complement the synopsis. Describe watching-feel; do not retell plot.
sections.relationship_with_moods_tags: Do not list tags. Turn the main feelings into plain mood-first language.

final_guide.analyst_notes: Active v3 = product-approved minimal mood-first guide (from v1.2 experiment). Mood named first; concrete film-owned after-clause; no pacing filler; no shared-medium 2D animation filler; Adj openings and repeated shapes OK.
